chunks: From him, from Ali ibn al-Nu'man, from Mu'awiya ibn Wahb, who said:

I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who sells a sale before he takes possession of it. He said: 'If it is not by measure or weight, do not sell it until you measure it or weigh it, unless the one who is in charge of it appoints a representative.'

key_terms.قَامَ عَلَيْهِ: who is in charge of it / supervisor

ai.seo_question: What is the condition for selling goods before taking possession in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) distinguishes between fungible goods defined by standard measure or weight, which may be sold prior to physical possession, and other goods requiring actual possession (qabd) to avoid uncertainty (gharar). This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle that for non-standardized items, the risk of loss remains with the seller until transfer, unless a designated supervisor (qaim 'alayh) ensures the specific goods are identified and secured for the buyer.
